// POSITIVE fixture for the G-10-4 Hole 1 lexer desync.
//
// A regex literal in expression position after `return`, whose body contains a lone apostrophe.
// The old stripper's regex-vs-division rule only looked at the last significant *punctuation*
// character, so the `n` of `return` failed the test and the `/` was read as division. The regex
// body was then scanned as code, the apostrophe flipped the lexer into single-quote string mode,
// and — because string mode ran to the next `'`, which never came — the whole rest of the file was
// blanked. Every ban below became invisible. The `??` on the last line is the proof.
export function isContraction(word) {
  return /don't/.test(word);
}

export function withDefault(value, fallback) {
  return value ?? fallback;
}
